config.title: Secure Token Rotation

intro.title: Secure Token Rotation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React component that securely rotates an authentication token at a set interval. You will learn how to use the useState and useEffect hooks to manage and update the token state over time. The core programming concept involves implementing a timer to trigger token updates while ensuring the component cleans up properly to prevent memory leaks. This exercise introduces you to secure token handling and side-effect management in React, key skills for building safe, dynamic web applications.
intro.usecase: Secure token rotation is essential in applications that handle user authentication and API security, such as banking apps, e-commerce platforms, and enterprise dashboards. For example, when you remain logged into your online banking dashboard while performing multiple transactions, the system automatically refreshes your session tokens in the background to prevent unauthorized access. Developers implement this pattern in login forms, admin panels, and data-rich interfaces where maintaining secure, uninterrupted user sessions is critical. This ensures that sensitive operations—like updating payment methods or accessing confidential reports—remain protected against token theft or expiration without disrupting the user experience.

objectives: Implement a React component that manages authentication token state
Configure token refresh intervals using React hooks
Construct API request functions that handle token rotation
Apply conditional rendering based on token validity status
Integrate token refresh logic with API call handlers
Initialize secure token storage using browser session mechanisms
Manipulate component state to reflect token rotation lifecycle

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TokenRotationApp that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax, and make it return a JSX div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the TokenRotationApp component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The TokenRotationApp component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named TokenRotationApp is created and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly TokenRotationApp and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it TokenRotationApp and it returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize token state
steps.instruction: Inside the TokenRotationApp component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'accessToken' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into a variable and a setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for user input
const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable 'accessToken' initialized to an empty string, ready to store the current token value.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string initial value, and the returned array is destructured into 'accessToken' and 'setAccessToken' variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with an empty string initial value and destructuring the result into two variables: the first should be named 'accessToken'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the component, use useState('') to create a state variable named 'accessToken'.

steps.title: Initialize refresh token state
steps.instruction: Inside your TokenRotationApp component, use useState to create a state variable named 'refreshToken' with an initial value of 'initial-refresh-token'.
steps.hint: Add a second useState call similar to your accessToken state, but name the variable 'refreshToken' and set its initial value to the string 'initial-refresh-token'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating another state variable
const [username, setUsername] = useState('guest');
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: accessToken for the access token and refreshToken for the refresh token, both initialized with placeholder values.
successCriteria: A state variable named 'refreshToken' is created using useState with an initial value of 'initial-refresh-token'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using useState to create a variable named 'refreshToken' with the exact initial value 'initial-refresh-token'.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a useState call inside your component to create a state variable named 'refreshToken' with initial value 'initial-refresh-token'.

steps.title: Define the rotateToken function
steps.instruction: Inside the TokenRotationApp component, define an async function named rotateToken that will handle secure token rotation.
steps.hint: Start by writing 'async function rotateToken() {}' or 'const rotateToken = async () => {}' inside your component, before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an async rotateToken function defined inside your component (though it won't do anything yet).
successCriteria: The component contains an async function named rotateToken defined before the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined an async function named rotateToken inside the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined an async function named rotateToken inside the TokenRotationApp component.

successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element with className='token-container' wrapping the h1 element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a div with className='token-container' that wraps the h1 element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you replaced the existing div with a new div that has className='token-container' and contains the h1.

steps.title: Display current access token
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your component, add a paragraph element that displays the current accessToken state value with appropriate labeling text.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to embed the accessToken state variable inside the paragraph text.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the accessToken state value with appropriate labeling text.

steps.title: Add rotate button with click handler
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Rotate Token' and wire its onClick event to call the rotateToken function.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick handler that references your rotateToken function.
steps.analogousExample:

<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Rotate Token' appears in the UI that will trigger the token rotation when clicked.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Rotate Token' and onClick handler calling rotateToken is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check that it has the correct text and onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button with onClick handler is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Display loading state
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering that shows 'Rotating token...' when isLoading is true, otherwise show nothing.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally render a paragraph element based on the isLoading state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a loading message only when the token rotation is in progress, providing visual feedback to the user.
successCriteria: A ternary operator conditionally renders a paragraph with the text 'Rotating token...' when isLoading is true, and renders nothing when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using the isLoading state correctly in the ternary operator and rendering the paragraph with the exact text 'Rotating token...'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering for the loading state isn't working as expected. Make sure you're using a ternary operator with isLoading and rendering the paragraph only when true.
